input.rationale: Read the retained receipt of experiment 03d8630fd2a64384a825524b28696d36-experiment (CheckRun f418b9d6ab8841faa9ab6c35ce1fcd75): setup event 6 shows the restarted node's live configuration empty (log-recorded configuration holds one voter, derived quorum size 1) and result event 7 shows that node granting both RequestVote and RequestPreVote to a candidate absent from its configuration. The child question therefore moves to a witnessed violation, with the receipt recorded as a behavior entry. The next judgment-changing step registered here is the safety consequence of a stale (rather than empty) configuration: whether a restarted node commits with a quorum that is not a majority of the configuration in force, so that an acknowledged write can be superseded.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the empty configuration also changes the node's own participation (runFollower election gating) and whether the node accepts AppendEntries from the requester as its leader, both measured rather than derived.

investigations.question: Does a node restarted with a stale (smaller) configuration after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart commit entries with a quorum that is not a majority of the configuration in force, so that a write acknowledged to a client can be superseded by a leader elected from the true configuration?
investigations.hypothesis: r.configurations.latest, commitment.setConfiguration and quorumSize() all use the recovered configuration, so a stale restarted node can win an election against the stale voter set and commit an entry with acknowledgements from fewer than a majority of the true configuration; those holders can then be removed from service while a true majority elects a leader whose log lacks the entry.
investigations.discriminator: Build a five-voter cluster whose commit-tracking stores are retained, take a snapshot on one follower while the configuration is still the three-voter set, commit the configuration change that adds the other two voters plus later commands on that follower, restart it (stale configuration), remove the serving leader and the two voters not in the stale set so that the stale quorum is reachable, apply a write and record its future result, then remove the stale leader and its acknowledgement partner, restart the remaining voters and record whether the new leader's log and FSM contain the acknowledged write.

knowledge.statement: A node whose configuration is empty after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart still answers RequestVote and RequestPreVote with Granted=true for a candidate that appears in no configuration, because both handlers apply their membership rejection only when the candidate's own Servers list is non-empty; the node also adopts the requester's higher term and derives a quorum size of 1 from the empty voter list.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a commit-tracking store; the node restarts with no snapshot so its configuration is empty after NewRaft; the requester's term is higher and its last log entry is at least as recent as the node's; the request is delivered over the transport.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: the empty configuration produced by a RestoreCommittedLogs restart removes the membership admission check from vote and pre-vote handling, and the retained execution shows the resulting admission of a non-member. Parsed event 6 (setup): live_config_after_restart is empty with live_voters 0 and derived_quorum_size 1, while log_recorded_config still holds the one bootstrapped voter, so the configuration in force (recorded in the node's own log) is not what the node uses. Parsed event 7 (result, same node and configuration): request_vote_granted=true with request_vote_term 3, request_prevote_granted=true with request_prevote_term 4, candidate_in_live_config=false, node_term_after_requests 3 - that is, a candidate appearing in no configuration was granted a vote and a pre-vote, and the node adopted the requester's higher term. Both declared comparisons are violated at index 7. Mechanism from source: requestVote and requestPreVote reject candidates outside the configuration only when the handler's own Servers list is non-empty, a leniency documented for the bootstrap case, so an empty list accepts any candidate; quorumSize() over the empty voter list yields 1. Consequence boundaries: the requester's log was made at least as recent as the node's, so no recency rule applied, and the restarted node has no known leader after its own recovery, so the leader-availability rejection did not apply either; the node's own election gating (runFollower aborting when no peers are known) is source-derived, not measured, and is left as the next discriminator.
counterevidence: Granting a vote when the configuration is empty is intentional behaviour for a cluster that is being bootstrapped; the defect here is that the node's own recovery path leaves the configuration empty in a cluster that is not being bootstrapped, not the leniency itself.

The probe supplied a candidate whose log was at least as recent as the node's and whose term was higher, which is what makes the vote grant observable; a stale or older candidate would still be rejected by the log-recency rules.
The same configuration gap is repaired by any later configuration entry or installed snapshot, so a healthy cluster with continuing traffic repairs the node without operator action.
limitations: Measured on a single-node in-memory cluster with snapshotting disabled and the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore, with the candidate reaching the node through the in-memory transport.

Only RequestVote and RequestPreVote admission was driven; whether the node accepts AppendEntries or accepts leadership from a non-member, and whether its own candidacy is suppressed, is not measured here.
The node adopted the requester's term, but no consequence of that term change (for example disruption of an existing leader) was measured.

investigations.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled, does the NewRaft configuration scan still load every committed configuration entry at or below the commit index the node recovers, so that r.configurations reflects committed membership after restart?
investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the recovered commit index, and the scan loop starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so committed configuration entries at or below the commit index are never loaded into r.configurations; a restarted node keeps the snapshot configuration only, or an empty configuration when it has no snapshot.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a later configuration entry or an installed snapshot repairs the restarted node's configuration at runtime, and which requests the empty/stale configuration admits (vote and pre-vote membership checks, quorum size, election gating).

investigations.question: Can restoreFromCommittedLogs block NewRaft forever when the recovered committed range needs more FSM batches than the fsmMutateCh buffer, given that runFSM is only started after NewRaft's recovery completes?
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs sends commitTuple batches through a 128-slot fsmMutateCh while no consumer exists yet, so a recovered committed range larger than 128 batches (64 entries each by default) makes NewRaft block indefinitely.
investigations.discriminator: Restart with RestoreCommittedLogs and a recovered committed range larger than 128*MaxAppendEntries entries, and observe whether NewRaft returns within a bounded interval.

investigations.question: With an empty or stale configuration after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart, which admission checks does the node still apply to RequestVote/RequestPreVote, and what quorum and election gating follow from that state?
investigations.hypothesis: requestVote and requestPreVote skip the membership check when the candidate configuration is empty, so the restarted node grants votes to any candidate, and quorumSize() derived from an empty voter list is 1.
investigations.discriminator: Drive the restarted node's vote and pre-vote handlers with a candidate that is absent from its log-recorded configuration and observe granted versus rejected responses.

knowledge.statement: With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft's configuration scan starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 after restoreFromCommittedLogs has set lastApplied to the recovered commit index; committed LogConfiguration entries at or below that index are therefore never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry, so r.configurations keeps the snapshot configuration or stays empty when no snapshot exists.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the node restarts from its retained log, stable store and snapshots; the configuration entry index is at or below the commit index reported by GetCommitIndex.

knowledge.statement: processLogs feeds r.fsmMutateCh in batches of MaxAppendEntries, while runFSM (its only consumer) is started only after restoreSnapshot/restoreFromCommittedLogs inside NewRaft; a recovered committed range needing more batches than the 128-slot buffer leaves NewRaft blocked in that batch send, and the blocked goroutine is visible as processLogs.func1 under restoreFromCommittedLogs under NewRaft.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a commit-tracking store whose recovered commit index spans more than 128 batches of authored entries, and no consumer started yet inside NewRaft.

history.statement: processLogs feeds r.fsmMutateCh in batches of MaxAppendEntries, while runFSM (its only consumer) is only started after restoreSnapshot/restoreFromCommittedLogs; a recovered committed range needing more batches than the 128-slot buffer makes NewRaft block in the send.
history.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, a commit-tracking store whose recovered commit index spans more than 128 batches of authored entries, and no consumer started yet inside NewRaft.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft's configuration scan excludes committed configuration entries. restoreFromCommittedLogs clamps the store's commit index and calls processLogs, which ends with setLastApplied(index); the following scan loop iterates from max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 up to the last log index, so any configuration entry with index at or below the recovered commit index is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. Both staging producers cap the staged value at entries already stored (raft.go:1266 for the leader, raft.go:1558 for followers), so the recovered commit index reaches a configuration entry whenever later entries were stored after it was committed. Consequence: the restarted node's r.configurations is the snapshot's configuration or, with no snapshot, empty, while its log reports that configuration entry as committed; an empty configuration makes runFollower abort elections (raft.go:232) and leaves the node's participant eligibility wrong until a later configuration entry or installed snapshot repairs it. Construction feedback: local, non-retained runs of these harness bytes reported variant A with last_applied_after_restart=11, config_scan_start_index=12, the bootstrap LogConfiguration at index 1 not covered and latest_config_after_restart_len=0; variant B reported the committed LogConfiguration at index 23 (adding nonvoter-B) not covered with the post-restart configuration reduced to the snapshot's single voter. Those local numbers are construction feedback only, so the conclusion stays conditional until the retained receipt of the queued experiment is read.
counterevidence: The recovered committed entries are still applied to the FSM (processLogs), and a node can still learn the current configuration from any later configuration entry or installed snapshot, so the omission can be repaired and does not by itself corrupt the FSM.

Snapshot-level configuration is loaded correctly by restoreSnapshot, so the omission only appears for configuration entries that sit between the last snapshot (or index 0) and the recovered commit index.
No captured test asserts configuration state after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart, so the captured suite neither confirms nor contradicts the omission.
limitations: The account applies only to nodes configured with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off, lastApplied equals the snapshot index and the scan range is unchanged.
The consequences on elections, quorum and participant eligibility are currently source-derived (hasVote and the runFollower election gate), not measured.
The exact reported field values and the runtime confirmation depend on the queued experiment's retained receipt.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft's configuration scan excludes committed configuration entries, and the retained execution shows it. restoreFromCommittedLogs clamps the store's commit index, applies the recovered range through processLogs (which ends with setLastApplied(index)), and the following scan loop starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so a configuration entry at or below the recovered commit index is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. Staging producers cap the staged value at entries already stored, so the recovered commit index reaches a configuration entry whenever later entries were written after it committed. Parsed event 0 (event restore_committed_logs_no_snapshot, receipt 5e1ce9aa430842d5a9325cfecbc885f6): staged commit index 11 equals lastApplied 11, scan start 12, the committed LogConfiguration at index 1 is outside the scan, and the node's latest configuration after restart is empty (length 0) although before restart it held one voter and the FSM had been fed up to index 11. Parsed event 1 (restore_committed_logs_snapshot_and_config_change, same receipt): snapshot index 22 with configuration index 1, committed LogConfiguration at index 23 adding nonvoter-B, staged commit index 32 equals lastApplied 32, scan start 33, the entry is outside the scan, and the post-restart configuration is again only the snapshot's single voter, so the committed nonvoter is absent. Requirement contradicted by both witnesses: the restarted node's configuration state does not include every committed configuration entry. Source-derived consequences, not measured here: runFollower aborts elections when the configuration is empty (raft.go:232), quorumSize() returns 1 for an empty voter list, and requestVote/requestPreVote skip the membership rejection when the candidate configuration has no servers.
counterevidence: The recovered committed entries are still applied to the FSM, and any later configuration entry or an installed snapshot restores the node's configuration, so the omission is repaired by normal traffic in a healthy cluster.
Snapshot configuration is loaded correctly by restoreSnapshot, so the defect needs a committed configuration entry between the last snapshot (or index 0) and the recovered commit index.
No captured test asserts configuration state after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart, so the captured suite neither contradicts nor covers this path.
limitations: The account applies to nodes configured with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off lastApplied equals the snapshot index and the scan range is unchanged.

The executed cases used a single-node in-memory cluster with authored commands and the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore; behaviour for multi-node clusters, monotonic stores and production stores is not measured.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: a RestoreCommittedLogs restart cannot complete startup recovery once the recovered committed range needs more FSM batches than the 128-slot fsmMutateCh, because runFSM is only started after the recovery work that feeds it. The receipt shows both the boundary and the mechanism. Parsed event 3 (variant committed-range-entries-6001, 94 batches): NewRaft returned in 6 ms with lastApplied 6001, i.e. the same code path completes when the range fits the buffer, and that node's configuration after restart was empty (length 0), matching the separate configuration-scan account. Parsed event 5 (variant committed-range-entries-9001, 141 batches): no return within the 20000 ms bound, and the frames captured at that moment are goroutine 10 [select] github.com/hashicorp/raft.(*Raft).processLogs.func1 -> (*Raft).processLogs(index 0x2329 = 9001) -> (*Raft).restoreFromCommittedLogs -> NewRaft, created by the harness restart goroutine. No runFSM goroutine exists for that instance, so no consumer can drain the buffer and no repair is enabled by time alone; the only escape in that select is the instance's own shutdown channel, which nothing closes during construction. Conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs enabled with a commit-tracking store, and a recovered commit index whose distance from the last applied/snapshot index exceeds 8192 authored entries (128 batches of 64) - for example a snapshot gap larger than 8192 entries on a node that crashed before the next snapshot, or a node with snapshotting disabled. Fault assumptions: none injected; the block follows from the retained history produced by the node's own commit path.
counterevidence: The observation is a 20000 ms bounded wait, so the account claims a blocked startup under the stated conditions, not an infinite block proven for all time; a caller that closes the instance's shutdown channel could release the select.

The two cases differ only in the amount of authored history (6000 versus 9000 commands) and used a single-node in-memory cluster with an InmemCommitTrackingStore and snapshotting disabled, so the boundary is a batch-capacity property of NewRaft rather than a measured property of production stores.

The blocked range here was recovered from the same node's own log without any snapshot; whether a production restart reaches a range above 8192 entries depends on snapshot cadence and crash timing, which were not measured.
limitations: Applies only when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off, NewRaft never calls processLogs before starting runFSM.
The threshold is expressed in MaxAppendEntries-sized batches against the 128-slot buffer, so a configuration with a different MaxAppendEntries moves the boundary proportionally.
Interaction with the configuration-scan gap (both appear in the same recovery sequence) is not separated by this experiment; each is independently witnessed.

Parsed event 6 (setup): live_config_after_restart is empty with live_voters 0 and derived_quorum_size 1, while log_recorded_config still holds the one bootstrapped voter, so the configuration in force (recorded in the node's own log) is not what the node uses. Parsed event 7 (result, same node and configuration): request_vote_granted=true with request_vote_term 3, request_prevote_granted=true with request_prevote_term 4, candidate_in_live_config=false, node_term_after_requests 3 - that is, a candidate appearing in no configuration was granted a vote and a pre-vote, and the node adopted the requester's higher term. Both declared comparisons are violated at index 7. Mechanism from source: requestVote and requestPreVote reject candidates outside the configuration only when the handler's own Servers list is non-empty, a leniency documented for the bootstrap case, so an empty list accepts any candidate; quorumSize() over the empty voter list yields 1. Consequence boundaries: the requester's log was made at least as recent as the node's, so no recency rule applied, and the restarted node has no known leader after its own recovery, so the leader-availability rejection did not apply either; the node's own election gating (runFollower aborting when no peers are known) is source-derived, not measured, and is left as the next discriminator.
counterevidence: Granting a vote when the configuration is empty is intentional behaviour for a cluster that is being bootstrapped; the defect here is that the node's own recovery path leaves the configuration empty in a cluster that is not being bootstrapped, not the leniency itself.

The probe supplied a candidate whose log was at least as recent as the node's and whose term was higher, which is what makes the vote grant observable; a stale or older candidate would still be rejected by the log-recency rules.
The same configuration gap is repaired by any later configuration entry or installed snapshot, so a healthy cluster with continuing traffic repairs the node without operator action.
limitations: Measured on a single-node in-memory cluster with snapshotting disabled and the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore, with the candidate reaching the node through the in-memory transport.

Only RequestVote and RequestPreVote admission was driven; whether the node accepts AppendEntries or accepts leadership from a non-member, and whether its own candidacy is suppressed, is not measured here.
The node adopted the requester's term, but no consequence of that term change (for example disruption of an existing leader) was measured.
